newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas tumbles amid sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas tumbles amid sluggish trade.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were sharply lower Friday in both the domestic and export markets, pressured by a drop in industrial loads over the holiday.
Weekend prices at the AECO storage hub plummeted by more than C$1 to the C$2.20s and lower per gigajoule (GJ) after breaking through the $4 level on Tuesday.

"Industrial loads are off. It also wasn't as cold as some utilities thought it was going to be on the 24th, 25th and 26th," one Calgary-based trader said, adding many were withdrawing gas from storage to meet the heating demand.
However, temperatures are forecast to remain cold through at least the early part of next week, with temperature readings in Calgary as low as minus 38 degrees Celsius expected this weekend.
January AECO gas prices were talked around C$2.25 per GJ, up almost 20 cents from December's index.

At Sumas, Wash., the western Canadian export point, spot prices fell by about 15 cents to the $3.15-3.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area despite the continuance of below-normal temperatures and stormy weather in the Northwest.
These prices are down more than $1 per mmBtu from week-ago levels.
At Niagara, where temperatures were rising to above-normal levels, prices for the weekend lost an average of 25 cents to the $3.40s per mmBtu.

Adding to the bearish sentiment, traders said, was the faltering U.S. futures market, where NYMEX February Henry Hub was down 34.9 cents at $3.035 per mmBtu at 1452 EST after dipping to a low of $2.96.
